content: In the case of rabies, PEP is highly effective and involves a series of repeated injections of the rabies vaccine along with immunoglobulin. This treatment is critical following a bite from an animal suspected of being rabid to prevent the development of rabies, which is almost universally fatal once symptoms appear. The treatment course lasts for four weeks. While there is strong evidence supporting the effectiveness of PEP in preventing HIV infection, it is not infallible, and there have been documented cases of failure. The treatment regimen can be challenging to adhere to due to its side effects, which may include general malaise, fatigue, diarrhea, headaches, nausea, and vomiting. According to an Australian study, approximately two-thirds of individuals undergoing PEP reported experiencing mild to moderate side effects, while about one-quarter experienced severe side effects.
